The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, June 21, 1937
（批：D... 23 6 37）

Silk Mill Hands
Refuse To Return

Many Strikers Ignore
Order, Seek Trip
To Nanking
（批：LAB）

By this morning 80 per cent of the 2000 workers who walked out several days ago in protest against the police action in raiding a union headquarters and arresting some 40 members were still refusing to resume work. In the western mill area where four factories are affected, some 600 of the 800 strikers remain idle, while in Chinese controlled territory only 350 of the 1000 workers of the Mayar Ching Wei and number one mills are back at work.

Strikers this morning stated that they had sent 15 delegates to Soochow to prepare demands which will be submitted to the Government at Nanking, this method of holding meetings out of town having been adopted following the strong action taken by the local Chinese police against unions recently. Workers do not intend to resume until the Government has forced employers to carry out a compromise worked out by the Bureau of Social Welfare some time ago whereby old employees would be re-employed.
（批：cop/sih）

Meanwhile, further arrests have been made among the strikers. One woman was arrested in Nantao in front of the Mayar number one mill yesterday morning for alleged intimidation towards loyal workers while two men were taken into police custody this morning.

A short-lived strike took place at the Toyoda Cotton Mill because of the dismissal of 60 porters when a new contractor was employed. The walkout took place yesterday, but by this morning the old porters and contractor were back again. However, the men are making demands for increased wages now and other improvements in working conditions.

The Hwa Foong Flour Mill where serious rioting took place several days ago when new hands were hired to replace the strikers was working normally this morning after a compromise solution to the trouble had been reached through the mediation of the local Tangpu. Dismissed hands are each to receive a gratuity of $30. Some 60 men are affected by this decision, but the sum has not been paid as yet. When the mill reopened this morning, 186 workers reported.

Delivery coolies of the China Times of 130 Avenue Edward VII who declared a strike several days ago in protest against the dismissal of two of their number were back at work today, greatly subdued. The two were allegedly dismissed because they also delivered papers for rival newspaper offices.
（批：10/6 21/6）

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年6月21日，星期一
（批注：D... 23 6 37）

丝厂工人
拒绝复工

许多罢工者无视
命令，寻求前往
南京之行
（批注：LAB）

截至今晨，几天前为抗议警方突袭工会总部并逮捕约40名成员而罢工的2000名工人中，仍有80%拒绝复工。在受影响的四家工厂所在的西部厂区，800名罢工者中约有600人继续怠工；而在华界地区，美亚织绸厂（Mayar Ching Wei）及第一厂的1000名工人中，仅有350人返岗。

罢工者今晨表示，已派遣15名代表前往苏州起草诉求，随后将提交给南京政府。鉴于近期中国当地警方对工会采取强硬行动，工人们采取了这种在城外开会的方式。在政府迫使雇主执行社会福利局此前拟定的妥协方案（即复聘老员工）之前，工人们无意复工。
（批注：cop/sih）

与此同时，罢工者中又有更多人被捕。昨晨，一名妇女因被指控恐吓忠于职守的工人，在南市美亚第一厂门前被捕；另有两名男子于今晨被警方拘留。

丰田棉纺厂因雇佣新承包商而解雇60名搬运工，引发了一次短暂的罢工。罢工发生于昨日，但截至今晨，原搬运工和承包商均已复职。然而，工人们目前正提出增加工资及其他改善工作条件的要求。

数日前因雇佣新人替换罢工者而发生严重骚乱的和丰面粉厂，经当地党部调解达成妥协解决方案后，今晨已恢复正常运作。被解雇的工人每人将获得30美元遣散费。此决定涉及约60人，但该款项尚未支付。今晨工厂重新开工时，有186名工人报到。

爱德华七世大道130号《字林西报》（China Times）的送货苦力，数日前为抗议两名同事被解雇而宣布罢工，今日已复工，情绪大为收敛。据称，这两人被解雇的原因是他们同时也为竞争对手报社送报。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, June 19, 1937

Silk Strikers
Return To Jobs

Six Hundred At Work
Today, Concluding
Lengthy Strike

With their ringleaders detained at the Garrison Commander's Headquarters in Lunghwa and facing strict disciplinary action threatened by the Bureau of Police and Social Affairs and the City Kuomintang, more than 600 strikers of the Mayar Silk Weaving Factory returned to work at 6 o'clock this morning, concluding a walkout of many weeks marked by disorders and clashes with police.

The number of workers who resumed operation this morning represents but 50 per cent of the usual complement. Some strikers defied the orders while many are understood to be returning to Shanghai from their native homes and are expected to return within the next few days. The authorities had previously decreed that all of them must return before 6 o'clock this morning and those who failed to show up are automatically dismissed. All was quiet when the workers resumed this morning under supervision of large squads of Chinese police officers.

The conclusion of the silk weaving strike followed the onslaught on the Third District (Western Shanghai) Silk Weavers' Union off Brenan Road Wednesday night. That night, 40 alleged ringleaders of the labor agitation were arrested, bringing the total number of arrests in connection with the Mayar dispute to 50. Thirty-six of them were handed over to the Garrison Commander's Headquarters today to face the military tribunal. Four others were released. The 10 previously arrested agitators are also in the Lunghwa headquarters.

More than 100 workers, all members of the Union, yesterday called on the City Kuomintang Headquarters and requested the return of the union fittings, documents and furniture confiscated by the police Wednesday night. The Tangpu officials promised to discuss the issues with the police authorities.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年6月19日，星期六

丝厂罢工者
重返岗位

今日六百人复工，
结束漫长罢工

随着带头人在龙华警备司令部被拘留，并面临警察局和社会局以及市国民党部威胁采取的严厉纪律处分，美亚丝织厂（Mayar Silk Weaving Factory）的600多名罢工者于今晨6时复工，结束了持续数周、伴随混乱及与警方冲突的罢工行动。

今晨复工的工人数量仅占常规编制的50%。部分罢工者违抗命令，而据信许多人正从家乡返回上海，预计将在未来几天内归来。当局此前已下令，所有人必须于今晨6时前返回，未报到者将被视为自动解雇。今晨工人在大批中国警察的监督下复工，现场一切平静。

丝织罢工的结束，紧随周三夜间对位于白利南路（Brenan Road）附近的第三区（上海西区）丝织业工会的突击行动之后。当晚，40名涉嫌煽动劳工骚乱的带头人被捕，使与美亚纠纷相关的被捕总人数达到50人。其中36人于今日被移交给警备司令部，面临军事法庭审判。另有4人被释放。此前被捕的10名煽动者也关押在龙华司令部。

昨日，100多名工人（均为工会成员）前往市国民党部总部，要求归还周三夜间被警方没收的工会设备、文件和家具。党部官员承诺将与警方当局讨论这些问题。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JUNE 18, 1937

Ultimatum Is Issued Against
Silk Mill Strikers Here

All Idle Workers Must Return To-morrow Or Face
“Resignation Of Their Own Accord”; High
Authorities Are Confident Over Idea

With the arrest yesterday morning of the five ringleaders of local Chinese silk filature workers, who are alleged to have been behind all strikes called in recent months and who have long been wanted by the local courts on charges of intimidation and other offences, and more than 10 of their assistants, local Chinese authorities are confident that they have the situation in hand and have issued an order requiring all idle silk filature workers to return to work to-morrow before 6 o'clock. Those workers who refuse to do so will be held to have “resigned of their own accord.”

According to a reliable Chinese source, Wang Hou, alias Wang Shih-hsiung, for whom an order of arrest was issued by the Shanghai City Government long ago **〔此处转录不清〕** Chinese silk filatures have been troubled by numerous strikes, riots, and demonstrations is among the arrested persons. The other arrested ringleaders of the strikes are G. S. Sheng, F. Y. Hu, Tu Fah-sen and Yi Yeo-yung, all of whom have been serving with Wang as officers of the Third District Silk Filature Workers Union in the extra-Settlement road near Brenan Road. Wang is secretary of the union. They are all being detained at the headquarters of the Nantao Police Bureau.

The arrest of these men has evidently caused uneasiness among striking silk filature workers especially those of the Mayar Silk Works whose 10 factories were all forced to be closed more than a week ago on account of labour unrest. More than 1,000 of them yesterday morning protested against the arrest of their leaders and they besieged the Tessfield Village Sub-Station of the Nantao Bureau Police demanding the release of the arrested men. They also demanded the return of the documents seized at their union headquarters following the arrests. They were finally persuaded to leave the place by the police from Nantao headquarters, who explained to the workers that they had gone to the wrong station to petition.

Warning Order

In a strongly worded order jointly issued by the Nantao Kuomintang Headquarters and Bureau of Social Affairs yesterday morning workers were warned against further disturbances and required to return to work before 6 p.m. to-morrow. The order further stated that the Mayar Silk Works Company had been ordered to carry out an order issued previously by the Bureau regarding the treatment of workers including the increase of wages.

The order was issued at the instance of a petition from the management of the Mayar Silk Works in which a detailed report on a riot staged in the Nos. 1 and 2 factories of the company in Nahtao which forced the management to close all affiliated factories. It was alleged in this petition that on June 13 when about 400 workers had returned to work under official supervision some workers who were allegedly abetted by ringleaders of strikes went to the company on the pretext of returning to work but secretly forced those willing to work to quit. The stay-in strikers were also forced to fast as no food was available in the factories.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年6月18日，星期五

向本地丝厂
罢工者发出最后通牒

所有 idle 工人必须明日复工，否则面临
“自愿辞职”；高层
当局对此方案充满信心

随着今晨逮捕了五名本地中国缫丝工人的带头人（据称他们是近几个月来所有罢工的幕后策划者，且长期因地方法院以恐吓及其他罪名通缉），以及十多名其助手，中国地方当局确信局势已在掌控之中，并发布命令，要求所有闲置的缫丝工人于明日6时前复工。拒绝照做的工人将被视为“自愿辞职”。

据可靠的中方消息来源，王厚（别名王世雄），上海市政府早已对其签发逮捕令 **〔此处转录不清〕** 中国缫丝厂一直受到无数罢工、骚乱和示威活动的困扰，他是被捕人员之一。其他被捕的罢工带头人是 G. S. Sheng、F. Y. Hu、杜发森（Tu Fah-sen）和 Yi Yeo-yung，他们均与王一起在白利南路附近租界外马路的第三区缫丝工人联合会任职。王是该联合会的秘书。他们目前均被拘留在南市警察局总部。

这些人的被捕显然在罢工缫丝工人中引起了不安，尤其是美亚丝厂（Mayar Silk Works）的工人，该厂下属的10家工厂因劳工动荡于一周多前被迫全部关闭。昨晨，1000多名工人抗议逮捕他们的领导人，并包围了南市警察局提篮桥分局（Tessfield Village Sub-Station，音译：特斯菲尔德村分局），要求释放被捕者。他们还要求归还逮捕行动后在其工会总部查获的文件。最终，来自南市总部的警察说服他们离开，并向工人解释他们请愿找错了分局。

警告令

南市国民党部和社务局昨晨联合发布了一份措辞严厉的命令，警告工人不得进一步闹事，并要求于明日下午6时前复工。命令还指出，已责令美亚丝织公司执行社务局此前发布的关于对待工人的命令，包括增加工资。

该命令是应美亚丝织公司管理层的请愿而发布的，请愿书中详细报告了该公司位于南市的第1和第2工厂发生的骚乱，迫使管理层关闭所有附属工厂。请愿书声称，6月13日，当约400名工人在官方监督下复工时，一些据称受罢工带头人唆使的工人以复工为借口来到公司，却暗中强迫那些愿意工作的工人离职。留守罢工者也被迫禁食，因为工厂内没有食物供应。

Silk Filature Workers'
Unions Smashed, Chiefs
Are Held Under Arrest

Disbandment Ordered By Bureau Of Social Affairs
Following Recent Disturbances; New Groups To
Be Organized Under Kuomintang Leadership

WORKERS "RUN WILD" HELD RESPONSIBLE
FOR SHANGHAI LABOUR TROUBLES

Strong measures to quell growing disorganization in Shanghai's silk industry were taken yesterday by the Bureau of Social Affairs when an order was issued smashing up the silk filature workers' unions which were behind the recent strikes and disturbances at various mills here, and which are declared to have been directly responsible for the closure of numerous Chinese filatures and a costly burden to those which have managed to survive the disturbances.

Coincident with the disbandment of the old unions, Kuomintang Headquarters were requested to immediately organize another silk filature workers' union under Kuomintang leadership.

Leaders of the old unions were arrested immediately the closure order was issued according to Chinese reports last night, and a number of them appeared in the First Special District Court yesterday and were sentenced on sabotage counts.

Misled by inefficient union leaders, the silk filature workers had run wild, declared officials at the Civic Centre yesterday, and they had therefore been plunged into the recent labour troubles and disturbances.

Three Unions Closed

The decision calling for the closure of the unions was reached at a recent joint meeting held by officials of the Bureau of Social Affairs, Nantao Kuomintang Headquarters and Nantao Police Bureau. In accordance with this decision the Bureau issued the order yesterday.

The order affected three unions, the Preparatory Committee of the First District Silk Filature Workers' Union, the Third District Silk Weaving Factory Workers' Union and the Fourth District Silk Filature Workers' Union.

The Fourth District Silk Filature Workers' union, which is located in the Tsapkadoo district where many silk filatures are located, it will be recalled, was the scene of disturbances just over a week ago. Twenty-one leaders and members of the union were arrested by the Tulin Road police and subsequently sentenced by the First Special District Court. They were charged with having manhandled a woman who went to work during the disturbances as a strike breaker.

缫丝工人
工会被取缔，首领
被捕

社务局下令解散
鉴于近期骚乱；新团体将在
国民党领导下组建

工人“失控”
被认为应对上海劳工纠纷负责

社务局昨日采取强硬措施，以遏制上海丝绸行业日益严重的无序状态，发布命令取缔了幕后策划近期本地各丝厂罢工和骚乱的缫丝工人工会。当局宣称，这些工会直接导致众多中国缫丝厂关闭，并给那些在动荡中幸存下来的工厂带来了沉重的经济负担。

在解散旧工会的同时，已请求国民党部立即在国民党领导下组织另一个缫丝工人工会。

据昨晚中方报道，旧工会的领导人在解散令发布后立即被捕，其中一些人昨日出现在第一特区地方法院，并以破坏罪被判刑。

市民中心（Civic Centre）的官员昨日宣称，缫丝工人被效率低下的工会领导人误导，行为失控，因此陷入了近期的劳工纠纷和骚乱之中。

三个工会被关闭

社务局官员、南市国民党部和南市警察局官员在最近的一次联席会议上做出了关闭工会的决定。根据这一决定，社务局于昨日发布了命令。

该命令涉及三个工会：第一区缫丝工人联合会筹备委员会、第三区丝织厂工人联合会和第四区缫丝工人联合会。

值得注意的是，位于扎卡杜（Tsapkadoo，音译：闸北或特定区域名）区的第四区缫丝工人联合会，该地区拥有许多缫丝厂，就在刚过一周前发生了骚乱。该联合会的21名领导人和成员被图林路（Tulin Road，音译）警察逮捕，随后由第一特区地方法院判刑。他们被指控在骚乱期间殴打了一名作为罢工破坏者去上班的妇女。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MAY 19, 1937

Powerful Labour Ring
Is Aim Of Agitators
Throughout Shanghai

Police Check Silk Weavers' Organ Through Arrest
Of 21 Unionists For Intimidation And
Illegal Detention; Trial Today

PROMINENT FIGURES WORK BEHIND THE
SCENES TO WIELD NEW POWER

Special to "The Shanghai Times"

Behind the scenes of the widespread labour disturbances which have recently wracked Shanghai's principal industries—cotton, silk, transportation—are **〔此处转录不清〕** who are working for revolutionary changes which will radically affect the lives of many thousands. For several months past a small group of men, some of whom have been in the city over a long period of time, are aiming at the creation of a highly potent weapon—a labour organization which will embrace all fields from the small, home-industry type of business to factories employing thousands of hands.

This revolution, for it is a movement founded on force, has been long in coming. Modern industrial methods are comparatively new in China, and the labour organizations up to the present have generally been separate groups within factories, or at most controlling certain districts. This was due to the fact that much labour was formerly obtained through individual contractors, who were responsible for a certain group of hands. When strikes occurred, Settlement Police were usually able to settle the matter through mediating between the factory management and the labour contractor.

Changing Scene

But the scene has changed radically since the turbulent days of 1925 to 1927. The Chinese Government has come to be recognized as the paramount authority for maintaining law and order, and the Bureau of Social Affairs is its direct agent. Labour is more permanently fixed than in the early days, but with more certainty of employment there has also come a more embracing union movement. At present the silk weavers, the cotton weavers, the cigarette workers and others all belong to a rather loose knit organization. The separate branches act independently in strikes, but all contribute to a common food fund and especially for the support of parasitic groups at headquarters. This is a situation which probably will not exist for long, the authorities believe, for the advantages to be gained by those who can manipulate great masses of workers are too great to be overlooked.

Police Check Silk Union

Yulin Road Police last week hit at what is believed to be the hotbed of agitation among silk weavers in the Eastern District and arrested 21 leaders on charges of intimidation and illegal detention. They will face the First Special District Court this afternoon.

These men are leaders of one of seven silk weavers' organizations. They are not professional agitators or gangsters, but they are rapidly assuming the former status by virtue of their easy, parasitic existence. Such men are ripe material for sub-bosses under a central directing board.

Fifteen of this group are being charged with intimidation, while the remaining six are also charged with having forced Tsang Ziang-ling, a weaver, to the union in Chining Road on May 12, where they hung a sign around his neck, reading "a running dog of the Ching Shing Silk Filature and a traitor to the union."

They took a photograph of him kneeling with this sign around his neck, but police have located the photographer and it is believed that he will be able identify the ringleaders.

Another private action of a similar sort is pending against members of the same organization by an official of the Bureau of Social Affairs. They kidnapped him as he was trying to make mediatory overtures to strikers of the Ching Shing Filature.

Heavy Sentence Unlikely

These offenders can get a maximum of three years in gaol or a fine of $300 under the charges for which they are held, but it is thought unlikely that any severe sentence will be passed.

But it is not the individual cases which bother the authorities seriously—it is the steady move towards union combination which undoubtedly will play a decisive part in labour relations of the future.

《字林西报》，1937年5月19日，星期三

煽动者旨在上海各地
建立强大的劳工集团

警方通过逮捕21名工会成员查处缫丝工组织，
指控其恐吓及非法拘禁；今日受审

显要人物在幕后运作以施展新权力

《字林西报》特约稿

在最近席卷上海主要工业部门——棉纺、缫丝、运输业的广泛劳工骚乱背后，是**〔此处转录不清〕**，他们正致力于引发革命性变革，这将彻底影响成千上万人的生活。过去几个月来，一小群人（其中一些人在本市已逗留很长时间）一直旨在创造一种极具威力的武器——一个涵盖从家庭手工业式的小型企业到雇佣数千工人的工厂等所有领域的劳工组织。

这场革命，因为是一场基于武力的运动，早已酝酿多时。现代工业方法在中国尚属比较新鲜的事物，而迄今为止的劳工组织通常只是工厂内部的独立团体，或者最多控制某些区域。这是由于以往大量劳工是通过个体包工头招募的，这些包工头对特定的工人群体负责。当罢工发生时，租界警方通常能够通过调解厂方与劳工包工头之间的关系来解决事态。

局势变迁

但自1925年至1927年的动荡岁月以来，局势已发生根本性变化。中国政府已被公认为维持治安的最高权威，而社会局则是其直接代理机构。劳工队伍比早期更为固定，但随着就业保障性的提高，也出现了更具包容性的工会运动。目前，缫丝工、棉纺织工、卷烟工等均属于一个较为松散的组织。各分支在罢工行动中独立行事，但都向共同的伙食基金捐款，特别是用于支持总部那些寄生群体。当局认为，这种局面可能不会长久存在，因为那些能够操纵广大工人群体的人所能获得的利益太大，不容忽视。

警方查处缫丝工会

上周，榆林路警方打击了被认为是东区缫丝工煽动活动温床的组织，并以恐吓和非法拘禁罪名逮捕了21名头目。他们将于今天下午在第一特区地方法院出庭受审。

这些人是七个缫丝工组织之一的领导人。他们并非职业煽动者或流氓歹徒，但凭借其轻松寄生的生活状态，正迅速演变为前者。这类人是中央指导委员会下属小头目的成熟人选。

该团伙中有15人被控恐吓，其余6人还被控于5月12日强迫一名名叫曾祥林（Tsang Ziang-ling，音译）的织工前往济宁路（Chining Road，音译）的工会，在那里他们在他脖子上挂了一块牌子，上面写着“景星丝厂的走狗和工会的叛徒”。

他们拍摄了他跪地且颈挂此牌的照片，但警方已找到摄影师，相信他将能够指认主谋。

社会局的一名官员也对同一组织的成员提起了另一起类似的私人诉讼， pending（待决）。该官员在试图向景星丝厂（Ching Shing Filature）的罢工工人进行调解斡旋时被绑架。

不太可能重判

根据所受指控，这些违法者最高可得三年监禁或罚款300元，但人们认为不太可能判处任何严厉刑罚。

然而，令当局深感忧虑的并非个别案件，而是走向工会联合的稳步趋势，这无疑将在未来的劳资关系中发挥决定性作用。

Lack Of Materials Causes
Mayar Works To Close

Shortage Attributed To Strike Of Workers Of No. 1
Factory, Who Demand 10 Per Cent. Wage
Increase; Nanking Petitioned

Owing to lack of raw materials, as a result of the strike called by the workers preparing silk for weavers, the 10 factories of the Mayar Silk Works, the biggest of its kind in Shanghai, were forced to close their doors yesterday. The management of the filature has telegraphically petitioned the Nanking authorities to intervene as local officials have made futile mediatory efforts.

The closed factories had depended on the No. 1 factory in Da Pu Chiao, Nantao, for refining silk. Workers of this factory called a general strike three days ago explaining that they had failed to get a 10 per cent. increase in wages as ordered by the Bureau of Social Affairs, to which the management took exception. Since all other factories have used up their silk prepared by the No. 1 factory they could not continue their operations, according to the petition.

With the exception of the No. 4 and No. 9 factories which are located in Ferry Road and Sicca-wei Road respectively, all other factories of the filature are located in Chapel and Nantao. A notice announcing the closure of the factories was posted by the management last night alleging that the responsibility for the wholesale closure of factories should rest with the striking workers.

In their petition to Nanking, the management alleged that local officials had failed to arrest and punish the ringleaders of the various strikes suffered by silk filatures, and that as a result the ringleaders have become more malicious than ever. The strike called by workers of the No. 1 factory which, it was alleged, was instigated by the ringleaders, might deal a death blow to the filature, it was asserted. Similar petitions have been sent to the Bureau of Social Affairs and Nantao Kuomintang Headquarters explaining the reasons for the wholesale closure of factories.

Fresh labour troubles are looming in practically every silk filature and weaving factory as managements have refused to increase wages by 10 per cent. as was ordered. The filature managers have brought their grievances to the direct attention of the Shanghai City Government instead of the Bureau of Social Affairs, which ordered the increase trying to meet the striking workers halfway. The Bureau officials, however, still continued their mediatory efforts yesterday in persuading the strikers of the No. 10 factory of the filature to return to work.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, APRIL 3, 1937

STRIKES IN SHANGHAI

Information previously in the possession of those whose business it is to know such things that labour unrest was likely to be manifest in Shanghai this Spring is unfortunately proving to be true, for at the moment there are over 12,000 silk filature workers and about 3,000 cotton workers out on strike. It is pleasing, however, to learn that there are no immediate signs of the strikes spreading to any great extent, although, of course, it all depends on how the present situation is handled and whether wise counsels are going to prevail over the machinations of agitators. The use of that word "agitators" is deliberate in this connection, and is not a word we should use in reference to legitimate labour organizers—the responsible heads of properly-constituted Unions. In the case of both the silk workers and those employed at the Kung Yik Cotton Mill the demands being made are unreasonable, and have been so judged by the Bureau of Social Affairs which makes it its business to advise on the settlement of labour disputes. What has happened at the Kung Yik mill clearly illustrates the point. Although the workers there are better paid than in some other cotton mills of Shanghai and although a good many of them are known to be satisfied with conditions, the demand has been made that a blanket 30 per cent. increase in pay and some other concessions should be granted. The Social Bureau has advised that a 10 per cent. increase would be a more reasonable request, and the owners, viewing the attitude of the strikers as unreasonable, have been forced to declare what amounts to a counter lock-out, saying they will keep the mill shut until moderation is shown. In the case of the silk workers, regarding whom there has been trouble for a considerable time past, the Social Bureau recently "ordered" the workers back to work on terms which were held to be reasonably fair pending the discussion of other points, but there was the usual behind-scene intimidation and a general strike of filature workers was declared—or rather, imposed—on Tuesday night.

As was stated in this column yesterday in another connection, we are all in favour of labour being given its just and fair share of the profits of industry, and we also hold the belief, as must everyone else who is acquainted with conditions among the labouring masses of this country, that China is in need of nothing else quite so much as the raising of the economic status of the people. And if, because of a bumper cotton crop, rising world prices and a good demand for cotton products, the mills of Shanghai are in more profitable operation than they have been for a good while past, it is only fair that the workers, who have also been suffering by the depression, should be given an encouraging deal. But that is quite a different matter from the unrest which is apparently provoked by so-called labour leaders who are alleged to be unconnected with Moscow. The bogey of Moscow is, perhaps, all too often trotted out by labour-scared employers—but definite evidence is in the hands of official circles here to show that there is a direct link between current labour agitation and both financial and ideological inspiration from the city of the Kremlin. The knowledge that labour unrest was being planned has proved to be true, and the corollary already indicated must, unfortunately, be regarded as also true. Preachers are at work, organization lies in the background, and any sign of weakness in the face of such intimidation would undoubtedly be further exploited and the general situation made to go from bad to worse. For this reason it is to be hoped that the Chinese authorities, who have shown commendable strength in this matter of unreasonable labour demands in the recent past, will continue to give their support on the side of fair-minded employers and do their own counter-propaganda in the interests of industrial harmony. We do not think there is any need for alarmist fears, but there is need for wise counsel and the exercise of good guidance by those best placed to offer it. One can only hope that the present strikes will be quickly settled before the disaffection spreads to other concerns.

All over the world within recent months there has been agitation and movement by labour for better conditions. France has been through a serious phase of sit-down strikes, America is going through it now, there are labour demands in Britain, and in practically every country of the world there is ferment on the labour side of industry. The use of the strike weapon for the securing of fair conditions is a perfectly legitimate thing, but a very big question has been raised of late by the growing connection between organised labour and Leftist politics of an ideological character. It is also not without misgiving that vast power is seen passing into the hands of the heads of great omnibus Unions, at the beck of whose fingers many thousands of workers can paralyze the basic industry of a country. It is not only a question of wages which is being raised, but into whose hands is to rest the dominant political power.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年4月3日，星期六

上海的罢工

那些以了解此类事务为职的人此前掌握的情报显示，今年春季上海可能会出现劳工动荡，不幸的是，这一情报正被证实为真，因为目前已有超过12,000名缫丝工人和约3,000名棉纺工人罢工。然而，令人欣慰的是，目前尚无迹象表明罢工会大规模蔓延，当然，这完全取决于当前局势如何处理，以及明智的建议能否压倒煽动者的阴谋。在此语境下使用“煽动者”一词是刻意的，我们不应将此词用于指代合法的劳工组织者——即正式成立的工会的负责人。无论是缫丝工人还是公益纱厂（Kung Yik Cotton Mill）的雇员，其提出的要求都被认为是不合理的，负责就劳资纠纷调解提供建议的社会局也作出了如此判定。公益纱厂发生的情况清楚地说明了这一点。尽管该厂工人的薪资高于上海其他一些棉纺厂，且已知其中许多人对工作条件感到满意，但工人们仍要求普遍加薪30%并给予其他一些让步。社会局建议，加薪10%是更为合理的要求，而厂方鉴于罢工者的态度不合理，被迫宣布实行事实上的反向闭厂，表示在表现出克制之前将保持工厂关闭。至于缫丝工人，过去相当长一段时间内一直存在相关问题，社会局最近“命令”工人在讨论其他问题期间，基于被认为相当公平的条款复工，但幕后照常存在恐吓行为，周二晚间，一场缫丝工人的总罢工被宣布——或者更确切地说，是被强加——了。

正如本栏目昨日在另一话题中所述，我们都赞成劳工应获得工业利润中公正合理的份额，我们也持有这样的信念，任何熟悉中国广大劳工阶层状况的人都必须承认，中国最需要的莫过于提高人民的经济地位。如果由于棉花丰收、世界价格上涨以及对棉制品需求旺盛，上海的纱厂比过去很长一段时间以来的经营状况更加盈利，那么给予同样受经济萧条之苦的工人以鼓励性的待遇是公平的。但这与显然由所谓劳工领袖挑起的动荡完全是两回事，据称这些领袖与莫斯科并无关联。“莫斯科幽灵”或许常被害怕劳工运动的雇主们搬出来吓唬人，但官方手中确有确凿证据表明，当前的劳工煽动与来自克里姆林宫所在城市的资金和意识形态支持之间存在直接联系。此前获悉的关于劳工动荡正在策划中的消息已被证实为真，而不幸的是，由此推导出的前述结论也必须被视为属实。宣传人员正在活动，组织工作在幕后进行，面对此类恐吓若表现出任何软弱迹象，无疑会被进一步利用，导致整体局势恶化。因此，希望中国当局能继续支持持公平态度的雇主，他们近期在处理不合理的劳工要求方面表现出了值得称赞的力度，并为了工业和谐开展自己的反宣传。我们认为无需产生恐慌性的恐惧，但需要明智的建议，并由最适合提供建议的人施行良好的引导。人们只能希望目前的罢工能在不满情绪蔓延至其他企业之前迅速得到解决。

近几个月来，全世界范围内都出现了劳工为争取更好条件而进行的煽动和活动。法国经历了一段严重的静坐罢工阶段，美国目前正在经历，英国也有劳工要求，实际上世界上几乎每个国家的工业劳工方面都存在动荡。使用罢工这一手段来争取公平条件是完全合法的，但近年来，有组织的劳工与具有意识形态色彩的左翼政治之间日益紧密的联系提出了一个非常重大的问题。此外，看到巨大的权力落入大型综合工会领导人的手中，成千上万的工人随其指使即可瘫痪一个国家的基础工业，这也并非没有令人担忧之处。这不仅是一个工资问题，更是一个主导性政治权力将落入谁手的问题。

Parade Halted
In Yangtzepoo

LAST FLARE-UP

A parade of 750 workers from various silk filatures in Yangtzepoo and neighbouring Chinese territory briefly upset expectations of police yesterday afternoon that the strike situation had been entirely settled by the stern order of the Bureau of Social Affairs on Friday evening, ordering the workers to resume, pending negotiations between Chinese authorities and the various factory managements.

The parade, which started from Thorburn Road, was ill-timed, however, for the workers reached the Mei Foong Mill in Haichow Road at the same time as did police units, and the union delegates who demanded from the management a contribution towards their organization fund, were given short shrift. Two union men were arrested and the rest dispersed peacefully.

Promised a 10 per cent. increase in wages if they would return to work without further agitation, some 25 per cent. of silk workers in the three municipal areas were at their jobs yesterday morning. The remainder were expected to be working by Monday morning, following the usual last-minute argument which usually accompanies such a settlement. Of the 383 silk factories which have been on strike since Wednesday, 60 in the Settlement were operating yesterday and four in the French Concession.

The Yangtzepoo parade started at 3.30 and reached the Mei Foong Mill at about 4 p.m., to find police and several lorry-loads of the Russian S.V.C. members standing by. Several delegates got into the mill and demanded that the management pay something towards the union fund. They met with a flat refusal and were ejected.

There was some amount of argument outside the mill gates and then the crowd, upon advice of police, dispersed without noticeable trouble. Meantime, the 100 workers of the Mei Foong Company, a small organization, adjourned to their compound and were lectured by their foremen. The Reserve Unit stood by for several hours but no further demonstrations were attempted.

昨天下午，来自杨树浦及邻近华界各缫丝厂的750名工人举行游行，短暂打破了警方此前因社会局周五晚下达严厉命令、要求工人在中国当局与各工厂管理层谈判期间复工而认为罢工局势已完全平息的预期。

然而，这次从韬朋路（Thorburn Road）出发的游行时机不当，当工人到达海州路的美丰纱厂时，警察部队也同时抵达，向管理层要求为其组织基金捐款的工会代表遭到了冷遇。两名工会成员被捕，其余人和平散去。

在承诺若不再进行煽动并复工将加薪10%后，公共租界三个区域中约25%的缫丝工人昨天上午已回到工作岗位。预计其余工人将在周一上午复工，这通常伴随着此类和解过程中常见的最后一刻的争论。在自周三以来罢工的383家缫丝厂中，昨天有60家在租界内运营，4家在法租界内运营。

~~土星弧承认~~（原文不清或乱码，保留原意标注）
杨树浦的游行于3:30开始，约下午4点到达美丰纱厂，发现警察和几卡车的俄国义勇队（S.V.C.）成员在一旁待命。几名代表进入工厂，要求管理层向工会基金支付款项。他们遭到断然拒绝并被驱逐。

工厂门外发生了一些争执，随后在警方的劝告下，人群在没有明显骚乱的情况下散去。与此同时，美丰公司这家小型机构的100名工人回到厂区，听取了工头的训话。后备队在一旁待命数小时，但未再发生进一步的示威活动。

警方认为，这次游行仅仅是最后的爆发，是工会领导人在服从中国当局正式命令前的一种“保全面子”的安排。周四发生骚乱的公益纱厂（Kang Yih Cotton Mill，注：此处英文拼写与上文Kung Yik略有不同，依原文译出）的罢工状况仍在持续，昨天仍有3,000名工人被拒于厂外。申新纱厂（Sing Yue Cotton Mill）未能说服其2,500名工人复工，而ABC纱厂也已关闭。浦东天章厂（Tien Tsang firm）夜班的一百名工人昨天加入了同等数量的日班工人行列。他们要求恢复最近的减薪并给予加薪。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, APRIL 2, 1937

12,000 Silk Strikers Still
Restive Here Yesterday

No Major Disturbances Reported, But Requests Are
Sent To Bureau; Silk Merchants Take Stand
And Urge Harsh Strike Block

Refusing to call off their general strike, more than 12,000 workers of all Chinese silk filatures in Shanghai remained restive yesterday. They held meetings and sent petitioners to various Government organizations asking that the Bureau of Social Affairs rescind its order offering a 10 per cent. increase of wages as a condition for settling the strike that must be accepted by silk merchants and their striking workers. No major disturbances were reported.

While the strikers demanded a 20 per cent. wage increase, the Bureau officials tried to meet them half-way in their order, which also forbade workers to demand anything in connection with the question of wage increase. The petitioning workers, numbering more than 100, went to the Bureau in the morning, but Mr. Hsu Yar-fu, a department head, told them that it was impossible for the Government to withdraw the order. A written petition was also sent to the Bureau.

Silk merchants also took a firm attitude. They held meetings yesterday to discuss the Bureau order and, as a result, they petitioned the Bureau requesting the officials to stop mediation and to employ "effective" methods to prevent workers from calling strikes. They also appealed to the police of the three Municipalities asking that their property be protected.

Official Promise Given

At a press interview, Mr. Hsu Yar-fu stated that the workers should return to work after having been officially promised a wage increase of 10 per cent. Should they defy the order, they would be dealt with according to law. He regretted that the Bureau order, which was issued after careful consideration had been given by Mr. Pan Kung-chan, Commissioner of the Bureau, had been misunderstood. Besides promising the wage increase, the workers were given other financial advantages, including payment of wages on national holidays, etc.

Eight men arrested for disturbances in the Wayside District of the Settlement on Wednesday were brought before the First District Court yesterday and charged with offence against public order. One of the men proved to be a carpenter, and claimed to have had nothing to do with stoning a policeman and attempting to intimidate workers. Hearings were remanded until next week.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年4月2日，星期五

12,000名缫丝罢工工人
昨日在此仍不安定

未报告重大骚乱，但请愿书已
送至社会局；丝商采取立场
并敦促严厉封锁罢工

拒绝取消总罢工，上海所有华资缫丝厂的12,000多名工人昨天仍处于不安状态。他们举行集会，并向各政府机构派出请愿代表，要求社会局撤销其命令，该命令提出加薪10%作为解决罢工的条件，丝商及其罢工工人必须接受此条件。未报告发生重大骚乱。

虽然罢工者要求加薪20%，但社会局官员在其命令中试图采取折中方案，该命令还禁止工人就加薪问题提出任何其他要求。上午，100多名请愿工人前往社会局，但该局局长徐雅夫（Hsu Yar-fu，音译）先生告诉他们，政府不可能撤回该命令。一份书面请愿书也被送往社会局。

丝商也采取了强硬态度。他们昨天举行会议讨论社会局的命令，结果向该局提交请愿书，请求官员停止调解，并采用“有效”方法防止工人发动罢工。他们还向三个市政当局的警察发出呼吁，要求保护他们的财产。

官方作出承诺

在一次新闻采访中，徐雅夫先生表示，工人在官方承诺加薪10%后应当复工。如果他们违抗命令，将依法处置。他对社会局的命令被误解表示遗憾，该命令是在社会局局长潘公展（Pan Kung-chan）先生仔细考虑后发布的。除了承诺加薪外，工人还获得了其他经济利益，包括在国定假日支付工资等。

周三因在租界越界筑路区（Wayside District）制造骚乱而被捕的八名男子昨天被提审至第一特区法院，被控犯有扰乱公共秩序罪。其中一人证明自己是木匠，声称与投石袭击警察和试图恐吓工人无关。听证会延期至下周。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, APRIL 1, 1937.

Mill Strikers
Stone Police
In Two Riots

Clash With Settlement
Officers In Wayside;
Chinese In Nantao

DEADLOCK CONTINUED
AT CONFERENCE

Ten Per Cent. Increase Is
Rejected By Workers In
Meeting Last Night

Striking silk filature workers clashed with both Settlement and Chinese police in brushes yesterday morning, but the remainder of the day passed off without serious incident and late last night the situation in the affected areas was reported to be satisfactory. The clash with the Settlement police occurred at Wayside, where a smart response was made to a call put in by a Chinese constable when he was attacked by strikers, and eight of the rioters were arrested.

The incident took place at about 9.30 a.m., when some 300 strikers assembled outside the Yung Tseong Silk Filature on East Yuhang Road and attempted to intimidate workers there. A Chinese policeman intervened and was man-handled by a group of the strikers, being further attacked when he tried to put in a call for assistance from Wayside Station. The call was eventually put through and the rioters were dispersed after meeting the police with a barrage of stones and rubbish.

Almost all of the silk filatures located in the International Settlement, French Concession, Nantao and Chapei, were at a standstill yesterday as a result of the general strike called by the silk filature workers union at their meeting on Tuesday evening, following the breakdown of the negotiations with the employers for an increase in wages.

Only a few of the small filatures scattered in alleyways and in specially converted houses were reported to be working yesterday; and even these were ordered to stop by the 12,000 striking male and female workers.

Two Chinese police officers were hurt and their uniforms torn, many strikers received minor injuries and two trucks were badly damaged early yesterday morning when more than 500 striking workers tried to force their way into the main mill of the Mayar Silk Works in Hui Tung Road, Nantao, to persuade workers there to join in the walk-out. Seventeen were arrested but were released after official mediatory efforts had been made.

Trouble flared up late on Tuesday night when the representatives of all Shanghai silk filatures decided to declare a general strike. They were alleged to have tried to force men remaining at work to join them and at about 1 a.m. yesterday more than 500 of their number gathered around the main mill of the Mayar Silk Works. Despite the efforts of the police they tried to break into the mill.

Two trucks loaded with goods were trying to leave the mill when the workers attempted to force their way into the mill. The chauffeurs of the trucks were manhandled and the trucks were badly damaged with stones and other weapons.

A policeman tried to stop the workers but was driven away and his uniform was torn in several places. Another officer who was hurt had his coat stolen, it was reported.

There was every possibility that the trouble would be augmented as official efforts to settle the matter again resulted in a deadlock last night. Officials of the Bureau of Social Affairs and Nantao Kuomintang Headquarters tried to meet the striking workers half-way by requesting that their wages be increased by 10 per cent. and that they should return to work to-day.

This offer however, did not satisfy the strikers, who at a meeting held yesterday morning demanded an increase of at least 20 per cent.

《字林西报》，1937年4月1日，星期四。

缫丝厂罢工者
向警察投石
引发两起骚乱

在韦斯特路（Wayside）与租界
巡捕发生冲突；
南市发生华人冲突

会议陷入僵局

工人在昨晚会议上
拒绝百分之十的加薪

昨日清晨，罢工缫丝厂工人与租界及中国警察发生小规模冲突，但当日余下时间未发生严重事件，深夜据报道受影响地区的局势令人满意。与租界巡捕的冲突发生在韦斯特路（Wayside），当时一名华捕遭到罢工者袭击并请求支援，警方迅速响应，八名暴徒被捕。

事件发生在上午9时30分左右，约300名罢工者聚集在东余杭路永成缫丝厂外，试图恐吓该厂工人。一名华警介入干预，遭到一群罢工者的殴打，当他试图向韦斯特路巡捕房打电话求助时，又遭到进一步攻击。电话最终接通，暴徒们用石块和垃圾向警察猛掷，随后被驱散。

由于缫丝业工会在周二晚间会议上因与资方关于增加工资的谈判破裂而号召总罢工，昨日位于公共租界、法租界、南市和闸北的几乎所有缫丝厂均陷入停顿。

据报道，昨日只有少数散布在弄堂里和 specially converted houses（特别改建的房屋）中的小缫丝厂仍在开工；但这部分工厂也被12,000名男女罢工工人勒令停工。

昨日清晨，500多名罢工工人试图强行进入位于南市汇通路美亚织绸厂的主厂房，以说服该厂工人加入罢工行列，导致两名华警受伤，制服被撕破，许多罢工者受轻伤，两辆卡车严重受损。17人被捕，但在官方进行调解努力后获释。

周二深夜，当上海所有缫丝厂的代表决定宣布总罢工时，事态升级。据称他们试图强迫仍在工作的工人加入他们，昨日凌晨1点左右，500多名罢工者聚集在美亚织绸厂主厂房周围。尽管警察尽力阻止，他们仍试图闯入工厂。

当工人试图强行进入工厂时，两辆装载货物的卡车正试图离开工厂。卡车司机遭到殴打，卡车被石块和其他武器严重损坏。

据报道，一名警察试图阻止工人，但被赶走，制服多处被撕破。另一名受伤的警官外套被盗。

由于官方再次解决此事的努力于昨晚陷入僵局，事态极有可能进一步恶化。社会局官员和南市国民党总部试图采取折中方案，要求将工资提高10%，并让工人今日复工。

然而，这一提议并未满足罢工者的要求，他们在昨日早晨举行的会议上要求至少加薪20%。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 31, 1937.
15,000 Workers Strike
In Local Silk Mills;
Wage Increase Wanted

General Walk-Out Call-
ed Last Night After
Parleys Fail

MORE EXPECTED
TO JOIN TODAY

130 Plants All Over City
Affected; New Talks
Slated Today

Climaxing two weeks of inter-
mittent labor trouble punctuated
by sporadic bursts of violence, some
15,000 workers of Shanghai silk
weaving factories last night called
a general strike.

The walk-out, which ranks as
the most widespread in the year's
labor disputes, had already caused
the shut-down of more than 130
mills at midnight last night.

A large body of day-shift work-
ers, whose exact number could not
be determined last night, is ex-
pected to join the tie-up this
morning.

The decision to call the general
strike was reached late yesterday
evening following a deadlocked
"peace conference," which broke
up without achieving a compro-
mise after 6 p.m.

Mills All Over City

As a result of the serious labor
situation arising out of the strike,
the Ministry of Industry last night
instructed the Bureau of Social Af-
fairs of Greater Shanghai to work
for an early settlement of the
trouble. A special representative
of the Ministry was last night re-
ported to be coming here to take
part in the negotiations.

Silk mills affected by the tie-up
last night are scattered in the
city's three municipalities. Settle-
and Chinese police last night were
standing by, watching for any
sign of disturbance. No violence
was reported, however.

Last night's general strike came
as a result of a long-standing dis-
pute originating from the workers'
demands for shorter hours, increas-
ed wages and general improvement
in treatment.

Less than two weeks ago, strikes
in individual factories broke out.
At that time, it was evident that
unless some urgent steps were taken
the situation would lead to a
general flare-up.

To smooth over the trouble, a
mediation body was formed, con-
sisting of the workers' and employ-
ers' delegates, as well as officials of
the Bureau of Social Affairs and
Kuomintang Headquarters. This
organization was charged with the
duty of working out a compromise
satisfactory to both the workers
and the mill owners.

Wages Main Point

Successive "peace conferences"
were held but at none of these meet-
ings could an agreement be work-
ed out. As far as could be learn-
ed, the crux of the dispute seemed
to lie on the wage increase ques-
tion.

On the employers' side, it was
offered that all filature workers get-
ting at present wages below 50
cents a day would be given a 15
per cent raise. Those receiving more
than 60 cents per day were not to
be given any increase.

This offer was flatly rejected by
the workers' delegates who de-
manded the following schedule for
wage increases:
(a) Those getting below $1 per
day—30 per cent raise.
(b) Those getting above $1 per
day—15 per cent raise.
(c) Those getting $2 per day—
10 per cent rise.

Officials of the Bureau and the
Party who mediated failed to get
the two opposing parties to modify
their demands and offer. The con-
ference was deadlocked.

When news of failure of the
"peace conference" spread among
the mill workers, emergency meet-
ings were called to study tactics to be
taken. At 9.30 o'clock, the call
for a general strike was issued and
mills in the city closed one after
the other.

To Confer Today

Officials of the striking mill
hands, together with representatives
from various mills, are scheduled to
hold an emergency conference
this morning.

Court No. 5 at the First Special
District Court yesterday was crowd-
ed with persons coming to watch
the fate of the three silk filature
workers arrested Monday by
Yangtsepoo police. Their heads
were swathed in bandages.

One of the men had hurled a
large rock at Probationary Sergeant
M. O. Lovell and then tried to out-
sprint the officer. It seems that
the latter represented the police in
the athletic games here in 1935 and
he had little difficulty in catching
up with the worker.

All three were charged with
offenses against public order and
were each fined $30.

A short skirmish between police
of Yangtsepoo and hawkers oc-
curred yesterday morning near
Pingliang Road as a result of the
hawkers' failure to comply with a
police request to remove their mer-
chandise because licenses had not
been obtained. The trouble was
quickly finished and the hawkers
dispersed from the scene.

《大美晚报》，1937年3月31日，星期三。
15,000名工人
在当地丝厂罢工；
要求增加工资

谈判失败后
于昨晚号召
总罢工

预计今日
将有更多人加入

全市130家工厂
受影响；新谈判
定于今日举行

在经历了两周断断续续的劳工纠纷，并伴有零星暴力爆发之后，上海丝织厂的约15,000名工人于昨晚号召总罢工，达到高潮。

这次罢工是今年劳工纠纷中规模最大的一次，截至昨晚午夜，已导致130多家工厂停工。

预计大批日班工人将于今天上午加入停工行列，昨晚尚无法确定其确切人数。

在经历了一场僵持不下的“和平会议”后，于昨晚深夜做出了号召总罢工的决定，该会议在下午6点后未能达成妥协而休会。

全市各丝厂

鉴于罢工引发的严峻劳工局势，实业部昨晚指示大上海社会局致力于早日解决纠纷。据报道，实业部的一名特别代表昨晚正前来此地参加谈判。

昨晚受停工影响的丝厂散布在全市三个市政区域。租界和中国警察昨晚严阵以待，监视任何骚乱迹象。然而，未报告有暴力事件发生。

昨晚的总罢工是由于长期存在的纠纷所致，该纠纷源于工人要求缩短工时、增加工资以及普遍改善待遇。

不到两周前，个别工厂爆发了罢工。当时很明显，除非采取紧急措施，否则局势将导致全面爆发。

为了平息纠纷，成立了一个调解机构，由工人和雇主代表以及社会局和国民党总部的官员组成。该组织的职责是制定令工人和厂主双方都满意的妥协方案。

工资是主要焦点

接连举行了多次“和平会议”，但在这些会议上均未达成协议。据所知，争议的症结似乎在于增加工资的问题。

资方提出，目前日薪低于50美分的所有缫丝工人将获得15%的加薪。日薪超过60美分的工人不予加薪。

这一提议遭到工人代表的断然拒绝，他们提出了以下加薪方案：
(a) 日薪低于1美元者——加薪30%。
(b) 日薪高于1美元者——加薪15%。
(c) 日薪2美元者——加薪10%。

参与调解的社会局和党部官员未能使对立双方修改其要求和报价。会议陷入僵局。

当“和平会议”失败的消息在工厂工人中传开后，各方召开紧急会议研究对策。9时30分，发出了总罢工的号召，市内的工厂相继关闭。

今日将进行会谈

罢工工厂工人的官员以及各工厂的代表定于今天上午举行紧急会议。

昨日，第一特区地方法院第五庭挤满了前来旁听周一被杨树浦警察逮捕的三名缫丝厂工人命运的人。他们的头部缠着绷带。

其中一人曾向见习巡佐 M. O. Lovell 投掷一块大石头，然后试图跑得比警官快以逃脱。看来后者曾代表警方参加1935年在此举行的运动会，他毫不费力地追上了那名工人。

三人均被控犯有妨害治安罪，每人罚款30美元。

昨日清晨，杨树浦警察与小贩之间发生了一场小规模冲突，地点在平凉路附近，原因是小贩未能遵守警察因未取得执照而要求其移除商品的要求。麻烦很快得到解决，小贩从现场散去。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 31, 1937

General
Strike Of
Filatures

Situation In Local Silk
Industry Serious As
Talks Deadlocked

A decision to call a general strike
of all local silk filatures was arriv-
ed at at a meeting of representa-
tives of workers in the various
factories held at 9 o'clock yester-
day evening, following the break-
down of negotiations with employ-
ers held earlier in the day at the
Bureau of Social Affairs.
Notwithstanding the fact that a
general strike of all filatures was
called at 8 o'clock, as late as
midnight a number of factories in
the Yulin Road and Yangtsepoo dis-
tricts were reported to be operating
with night shifts.
An attempt to reach a settlement
was made yesterday by representa-
tives of workers and employers,
when discussions were held in the
presence of Mr. Pan Kung-chan,
Commissioner of Social Affairs.
Thirty common demands on a basis
of collective bargaining were pre-
sented. An agreement was reached
on almost all the demands with the
exception of that conceiving a
wage increase.
The trouble in silk filatures in
the eastern area had been brewing
for over a week and resulted in dis-
turbances on Sunday and Monday
afternoons. Three strikers, who
stoned officers of Yangtsepoo Police
Station on Monday, when the lat-
ter were dispersing them, were
fined $30 each in the First District
Court yesterday morning.
Most of the union workers were
on strike yesterday, but doubts were
expressed in certain quarters whe-
ther non-union workers would join
in the general walk-out.

缫丝厂
总罢工

随着谈判陷入僵局
本地丝绸业
局势严峻

在白天早些时候于社会局举行的与雇主的谈判破裂后，各工厂工人代表于昨晚9时举行的会议上做出了号召当地所有缫丝厂总罢工的决定。

尽管在8点钟已号召所有缫丝厂总罢工，但据报道，直至午夜，榆林路和杨树浦地区的一些工厂仍在进行夜班生产。

昨日，工人和雇主代表在社会局局长潘公展先生出席的情况下进行了讨论，试图达成和解。提出了基于集体谈判的三十项共同要求。除涉及增加工资的一项外，几乎对所有要求都达成了协议。

东部地区缫丝厂的麻烦已酝酿了一周多，并在周日下午和周一下午引发了骚乱。周一，当杨树浦巡捕房的警官驱散三名向警察投石的罢工者时，这三名罢工者于昨日上午在第一特区地方法院各被罚款30美元。

昨日大多数工会工人处于罢工状态，但某些方面对非工会工人是否会加入总罢工表示怀疑。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, MARCH 30. 1937

Silk Mill Hands
Stone Police in
Eastern District

New Trouble Quelled and
Three Men Arrested

OTHER WORKERS WALK
TO CHAPEI

Another clash between silk factory
workers and the Settlement Police
occurred in the Eastern district yes-
terday afternoon, resulting in the
dispersal of about 500 persons by
uniformed men and detectives from
the Yangtsepoo Station after the
mob had stoned the Police. No-one
was seriously injured in the en-
counter, which resulted in the Police
charging the crowd with batons at
Ying Ziang Kong, near Linching
Road.
The 500 workers, principally
strikers, went to the Yuan Ling Silk-
weaving Factory, 484 Linching Road,
at 1 p.m. in order to persuade the
workers there to join their union.
The strikers surrounded the grounds
and when the Police arrived they
threw stones, slightly injuring several
policemen. The crowd was dispersed
effectively at Ying Ziang Kong, near
by, and no attempt was made by the
demonstrators to form again. Three
men were arrested and taken to
Yangtsepoo Station.

Morning Demonstration

Earlier in the day, between 250 and
300 men and women workers, in-
cluding some of the strikers from the
Ching Shing Factory, Yulin Road,
had demonstrated in the Settlement
and Chinese territory.
These workers congregated at 10.30
a.m. in a vacant ground at the inter-
section of Ward and Whashing Roads
and then proceeded in groups, via
Ningkuo Road, towards the Civic
Centre. As they passed into Chinese
territory they formed a procession
and were joined by about 300 other
workers, mainly from the silk filatures
in Yangtsepoo. It was understood
they were headed towards the Mayar
Mills, where a "go-slow" strike is in
progress, as one of their destinations.
In Chapei, the workers held a meet-
ing in front of the Tomb for the
Victims of the May 30 Affair. De-
mands were drawn up calling for
better treatment for the workers and
for the prompt release of a striker
who had been taken into custody.
The Chinese Police were taking no
risks, however, and they promptly
interfered and dispersed the gather-
ing.

《华北每日新闻》，1937年3月30日，星期二。

丝厂工人
在东区向警察
投石

新麻烦被平息
三人被捕

其他工人步行
前往闸北

昨日下午，东区发生了丝厂工人与租界警察之间的另一次冲突，导致约500人被杨树浦巡捕房的制服巡捕和便衣侦探驱散，此前人群曾向警察投石。在这次冲突中无人受重伤，警察在林钦路附近的英商公记纱厂（Ying Ziang Kong，音译）用警棍驱散了人群。

这500名工人主要是罢工者，他们于下午1点前往林钦路484号的元隆丝织厂，目的是说服该厂工人加入他们的工会。罢工者包围了厂区，当警察到达时，他们投掷石块，致使几名警察受轻伤。人群在附近的英商公记纱厂（Ying Ziang Kong，音译）被有效驱散，示威者未再尝试集结。三人被捕并被带往杨树浦巡捕房。

晨间示威

当天早些时候，250至300名男女工人，包括一些来自榆林路庆兴工厂的罢工者，在租界和华界进行了示威。

这些工人于上午10时30分聚集在华德路与华盛路交叉口的空地上，然后分组经宁国路向市中心方向进发。当他们进入华界时，组成了游行队伍，并有约300名其他工人加入，主要来自杨树浦的缫丝厂。据悉，他们的目的地之一是美亚织绸厂，那里正在进行“怠工”罢工。

在闸北，工人们在五卅烈士墓前举行集会。他们起草了要求改善工人待遇并立即释放一名被拘留的罢工者的诉求。然而，中国警察不愿冒险，迅速介入并驱散了集会。

( The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, March 31, 1937

Silk Spinners
Out On Strike,
Thousands Idle

Hundreds Of Filatures
In City Close Down;
12,000 Quit Work

LABORERS DEMAND
INCREASED WAGE

Factories Paralyzed;
Mediation Fails;
Police Watch

There is no silk being spun in
Shanghai today.
The worst labor strike of the
year gripped the Settlement, Nan-
tao and Chapel last night and
swarmed over into Frenchtown to-
day. Twelve thousand silk work-
ers are idle; 230 silk mills, factor-
ies and workshops are shut down;
union leaders are making de-
mands, employers are rejecting
them, but no trouble has broken
out, and no rioting has occurred.
More Idle Expected
At 8:30 o'clock last night, the
workers of the Foo Yik Silk Mill
at 1032 Hart Road left their jobs
and set in motion a city-wide
strike for better wages and better
working conditions. Up to noon
today there were known to be 11,-
944 workers on strike from 220
mills, but this number will
probably be increased on the re-
ceipt of further reports.
The strike called last night
came as a result of the failure of
two weeks of protracted negotia-
tions and bickerings between silk
employees, employers and the
local Tangpu. On March 17, silk
workers called a mass meeting on
a piece of waste ground, and drew
up a set of demands which were
presented to silk mill owners. The
demands were not met, a long
series of negotiations followed,
with the Tangpu trying to act as
mediator.
Session Deadlocked
Last night, workers decided to
call a general strike when a well-
attended conference broke up with-
out achieving a compromise after 6
p.m.
As a result of this strike, the
following condition prevails:
Strikers Factories
Settlement
East. Dist. 4800 149
West. Dist. 575 7
Extr. Set. Rds. 515 6
Frenchtown 1500 20
Nantao 3000 10
Chapel 2000 8
In addition to the above known
number of strikers, there are
probably several hundred more
mill workers who will be affected.

Higher Wages Wanted
Up until the present time, no
outside influences have yet been
detected in the strike trouble and
it is held that the workers are
simply demanding higher wages
and better working conditions.
There is a union behind the strike
that originally is said to have de-
manded a 10 per cent blanket
raise. The management countered
with a refusal to grant a raise
to those workers receiving over
60 cents a day. This offer was
in turn rejected by the workers
who are said to have submitted
the following schedule for wage
increases:
(1) Those getting below $1 per
day—30 per cent raise.
(2) Those getting above $1 per
day—15 per cent raise.
(3) Those getting $3 per day—
10 per cent raise.
Mediation Fails
Officials of the Bureau of Social
Affairs and the local Tangpu who
mediated failed to get the two
parties to agree on a compromise
plan. Negotiations were deadlock-
ed.
Police of the three areas are
not on the lookout for any cases
of sabotage or any disturbances
that might conceivably take place
and it is reported that a repre-
sentative of the Ministry of In-
dustries has arrived in Shanghai
to try and settle the situation.

（《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年3月31日，星期三）

缫丝工人
罢工，
数千人闲置

市内数百家缫丝厂
关闭；
12,000人离职

劳工要求
增加工资

工厂瘫痪；
调解失败；
警方监视

今天上海没有丝绸在生产。
今年最严重的劳工罢工昨晚席卷了公共租界、南市和闸北，并于今天蔓延至法租界。一万二千名丝绸工人闲置；230家缫丝厂、工厂和作坊关闭；工会领袖提出要求，雇主予以拒绝，但尚未爆发冲突，也未发生骚乱。

预计更多人员闲置
昨晚8时30分，哈特路1032号福益缫丝厂（Foo Yik Silk Mill）的工人离开工位，发起了一场全市范围的罢工，以争取更高的工资和更好的工作条件。截至今天中午，已知有来自220家工厂的11,944名工人罢工，但随着进一步报告的收到，这一数字可能会增加。

昨晚发起的罢工是丝绸雇员、雇主与当地塘浦（Tangpu，音译）之间长达两周的冗长谈判和争吵失败的结果。3月17日，丝绸工人在一块空地上召开群众大会，并起草了一系列要求提交给缫丝厂主。这些要求未得到满足，随后进行了一系列漫长的谈判，塘浦试图充当调解人。

会议陷入僵局
昨晚，在一次出席人数众多的会议于下午6点后未能达成妥协而散会后，工人们决定发动总罢工。

由于此次罢工，目前情况如下：
罢工者 工厂
公共租界
东区 4800 149
西区 575 7
越界筑路 515 6
法租界 1500 20
南市 3000 10
闸北 2000 8

除上述已知的罢工人数外，可能还有数百名工厂工人将受到影响。

要求更高工资
到目前为止，尚未发现罢工事件中有外部势力介入，据信工人仅仅是要求更高的工资和更好的工作条件。罢工背后有一个工会，据说最初要求全面加薪10%。资方则以拒绝给日薪超过60美分的工人加薪作为回应。这一提议反过来被工人拒绝，据说工人提交了以下加薪方案：
(1) 日薪低于1美元者——加薪30%。
(2) 日薪高于1美元者——加薪15%。
(3) 日薪3美元者——加薪10%。

调解失败
参与调解的社会局官员和当地塘浦未能使双方就妥协方案达成一致。谈判陷入僵局。
三个区域的警方正在警惕任何可能发生的破坏案件或骚乱，据报道，实业部的一名代表已抵达上海，试图解决局势。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, MARCH 30, 1937

Trouble For
Filatures In
Eastern Area

Strikers Throw Stones
At Police; Three
Are Arrested

CROWD DISPERSES TO
CHINESE TERRITORY

Yulin Road, Yangtzepoo
Police Keep On Alert
Throughout Day

The trouble which had been brewing for the past week in the silk filatures in the Eastern industrial area, came to a head yesterday, with an attempt being made by some 300 workers to hold a meeting on a vacant piece of ground in the Yulin Road Police district in the morning, and the stoning of police officers of Yangtzepoo Police Station in the early afternoon, when they attempted to disperse a crowd of strikers, who gathered outside a filature on Linching Road.

The attempt to hold a meeting on a piece of vacant ground in Ward Road near Whashing Road at about 10.30 a.m. came as an aftermath to the trouble which occurred on Sunday afternoon outside the Ching Shing Factory at Lane 464, Yulin Road, when a detective was injured and one worker arrested.

The incident in the Yangtzepoo district, which occurred at 1 o'clock was of a more serious nature. Here a crowd of about 500 male and female silk filature strikers surrounded the Yuen Ling Filature at 484, Linching Road, with the idea of persuading the workers of the factory to join their union. The management of the factory immediately informed the Yangtzepoo Police and officers rushed to the factory.

In the meantime the 70 male and 50 female workers of the factory pointed out to the crowd outside that they did not wish to join the union. The police then told the crowd to disperse. They refused to do so, saying that their delegate was inside the factory. When it was ascertained that this was not the case, the crowd was again ordered to move. They retreated in the direction of the Chinese territory (Ying Ziang Kong) in the meantime throwing stones and bricks at the police. Officers charged the mob and three men were arrested. They will be charged in court to-morrow.

March To Civic Centre

The crowd which gathered on the piece of vacant ground at Ward Road and Whashing Road in the morning, was much more orderly, and persuasion on the part of the police resulted in the crowd, estimated at about 300, dispersing in small groups. They walked in small groups along Ningkue Road into Chinese territory. Once in Chinese territory they formed a procession, and, on being joined by another group of about 200 workers from the Yangtzepoo District, they started their march towards the Civic Centre.

The procession never reached the Civic Centre, but a meeting was held on the way and it was decided to march back into the Settlement and petition the management of the Ching Shing Filature to effect the release of the worker arrested on Sunday afternoon. In the alternative it was decided to march straight to the Yulin Road Police Station and demand that their colleague be released.

Shortly after the meeting at which this was decided upon, the crowd was dispersed by the Chinese Police. Officers of the Yangtzepoo and Yulin Road Police Station, however, were standing by throughout the day yesterday.

A large number of filatures in the Eastern area have been on strike for about a week. Yesterday, the number of the idle workers swelled due to it being a holiday, all union workers demanding a holiday on the occasion of the anniversary of the 72 Canton Martyrs of 1911.

Further disturbances are hourly expected in the Eastern area, pending settlement of the whole question. A set of demands have been presented by striking workers, but they are considered to be utterly out of the question.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年3月30日，星期二

东区
缫丝厂
出现麻烦

罢工者向警察
投掷石块；三人
被捕

人群疏散至
华界

榆林路、杨树浦
警方全天保持警戒

过去一周在东部工业区缫丝厂中酝酿的麻烦，于昨天达到高潮。上午，约300名工人试图在榆林路警区的一块空地上举行集会；下午早些时候，当杨树浦巡捕房警官试图驱散聚集在林钦路（Linching Road，音译）一家缫丝厂外的罢工人群时，遭到石块袭击。

上午10时30分左右，在华德路靠近华盛路拐角处的一块空地上试图举行集会的举动，是周日下午发生在榆林路464弄庆兴厂（Ching Shing Factory）外事件的余波，当时一名侦探受伤，一名工人被捕。

下午1时发生在杨树浦区的事件性质更为严重。当时，约500名男女缫丝厂罢工者包围了林钦路484号的元灵缫丝厂（Yuen Ling Filature），意图说服该厂工人加入他们的工会。厂方立即通知杨树浦警方，警官迅速赶往工厂。

与此同时，该厂的70名男工和50名女工向外面的人群指出，他们不希望加入工会。警方随后命令人群解散。他们拒绝这样做，称他们的代表在工厂内。当查明并非如此后，再次命令人群离开。他们朝华界（Ying Ziang Kong，音译，疑为“引翔港”或泛指中国地界）方向撤退，同时向警察投掷石块和砖头。警官冲向人群，逮捕了三名男子。他们将于明天在法庭被起诉。

走向市中心

上午在华德路和华盛路拐角处的空地上聚集的人群秩序要好得多，经警方劝解，估计约300人的群体分成小组散去。他们沿宁国路（Ningkue Road）成群结队地走进华界。一旦进入华界，他们组成游行队伍，并在另一群来自杨树浦区的约200名工人加入后，开始向市中心进发。

游行队伍从未到达市中心，但在途中举行了一次会议，决定返回租界，向庆兴缫丝厂管理层请愿，要求释放周日下午被捕的工人。或者，决定直接前往榆林路巡捕房，要求释放他们的同事。

就在做出这一决定的会议结束后不久，人群被中国警察驱散。然而，杨树浦和榆林路巡捕房的警官昨天全天都在待命。

东部地区的大量缫丝厂已罢工约一周。昨天，由于恰逢1911年广州七十二烈士纪念日，所有工会工人都要求休假，闲置工人的数量因此增加。

在整个问题得到解决之前，预计东部地区随时可能发生进一步的骚乱。罢工工人提出了一系列要求，但被认为完全不可行。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, MARCH 30 1937

Mill Workers
Dispersed By
Police Forces

Called Out To Break
Up Demonstrations;
Bricks Thrown

Several minor disturbances featured the situation on the Shanghai labor front with trouble in the silk filatures of the Settlement holding most of the spotlight. Two demonstrations occurred, one on a vacant lot at the corner of Ward and Whashing Road, and the other at the Yuen Ling Silk Filature, 484 Lincheng Road. Workers stoned the police during the latter affair.

At 10.30 a.m., about 300 men and women workers of the Ching Shing Silk Factory, 484 Yalu Road, who went on strike Sunday, gathered on a vacant piece of land off Ward Road near the corner of Whashing Road and attempted to hold an indignation meeting. They were dispersed by the police and moved off into Chapel where they were joined by workers from other filatures.

In Chapel, the group proceeded to parade up and down the streets, shouting slogans as well as expressions of their opinion of the filature owners. The Bureau of Police went into action and dispersed them. No injuries were reported either in the Settlement or Chapel.

Shortly after 1 p.m., the disunited workers managed to collect together again in a body and marched to the Yuen Ling Silk Filature, 484 Lincheng Road, and surrounded the place. The idea was to create a sympathy strike.

Police reserves from the Yangtszepoo Station were rushed to the scene and encountered difficulty in breaking up the strikers. The latter were prepared for the officers and let loose with a barrage of stones, bricks and other missiles. No serious injuries were reported on the side of the police.

The officers moved quickly despite the stones and dispersed the mob in short order. Three workers, believed to be agitators, were arrested.

Conditions at the Shing Yue Cotton Mills, No. 1 and No. 2, on Robison Road, scene of rioting last Thursday, remained quiet yesterday. The mills were reopened in the morning and all workers were back on the job.

《字林西报》，1937年3月30日，星期二

工厂工人
被警察部队
驱散

被召去驱散
示威活动；
有人投掷砖块

上海劳工战线出现了几起小规模骚乱，其中公共租界缫丝厂的麻烦占据了大部分焦点。发生了两次示威活动，一次在华德路和华盛路拐角处的一块空地上，另一次在林钦路484号的元灵缫丝厂。在后一起事件中，工人向警察投掷石块。

上午10时30分，亚尔路484号庆兴丝绸厂（Ching Shing Silk Factory）周日罢工的约300名男女工人聚集在华德路附近靠近华盛路拐角处的一块空地上，试图举行抗议集会。他们被警察驱散，并移动至闸北，在那里与其他缫丝厂的工人汇合。

在闸北，这群人在街道上来回游行，高呼口号以及表达对缫丝厂主的看法。警务处采取行动并将他们驱散。公共租界或闸北均未报告有人受伤。

下午1点后不久，分散的工人设法再次集结成群，游行至林钦路484号的元灵缫丝厂，并包围了该地。其目的是引发同情性罢工。

杨树浦巡捕房的后备警力被紧急调往现场，在驱散罢工者时遇到困难。后者对警官有所准备，投掷了大量石块、砖块和其他投射物。警方方面未报告有重伤。

尽管面临石块攻击，警官们迅速行动，很快驱散了人群。三名被认为是煽动者的工人被捕。

罗宾森路（Robison Road）上的申悦棉纺厂一厂和二厂，即上周四骚乱的地点，昨天保持平静。工厂上午重新开工，所有工人均已返岗。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, MARCH 29, 1937

Two Men Injured
As Strikers Rush
Yangtszepoo Mill

Office Damaged by Crowd
Seeking Manager

POLICE QUICKLY CLEAR
**〔此处转录不清〕**

Trouble broke out again on Shang-
hai's labour front yesterday afternoon
when the striking workers of the
Ching Shing Silk Factory, in Yang-
tszepoo, tangled with members of the
staff and the Police in the compound
of the establishment.
The disturbance, in which two men
were so seriously injured that they
had to be sent to hospital, started at
about 3 o'clock. At that time some
150 of the strikers, reinforced by the
loafer element, went to the factory
premises in Lane 484, Yulin Road,
and attempted to enter the compound
in order to speak to the manager.
Members of the staff tried to prevent
them from entering and at the same
time telephoned for Police assistance.
A fight ensued in the course of
which a foreman employed at the
mill and a Chinese detective-constable
from the Yulin Road Station were
beaten badly, while others suffered
less serious injuries. Some damage
was caused to the windows and furni-
ture of the office. A Police party
from Yulin Road finally dispersed the
crowd and cleared the premises,
arresting one man as a leader of the
disturbance. Quiet was quickly
restored and a Police watch placed
about the mill.
The injured foreman was taken to
the Sacred Heart Hospital and the
Chinese detective to the Police Hos-
pital.

Meeting Frustrated

Later in the afternoon the workers
attempted to hold a meeting on
vacant property at the intersection of
Whashing and Ward Roads. Another
turn-out of Police was made from the
Yulin Road Station, and the crowd
dispersed without hesitation.
The situation was quiet last night.
At the Sing Yue Cotton Mills,
where a lock-out exists, pending the
outcome of negotiations between dis-
gruntled workers and the manage-
ment, no developments were reported
yesterday. A disturbance occurred
on Thursday morning when a mob
of 800 forced the gate of the No. 7
Mill at 8 Robison Road, but yester-
day both mills were quiet.

D.S. O'Kearn.

《华北日报》，1937年3月29日，星期一

两名男子受伤
因罢工者冲击
杨树浦工厂

寻求经理的
人群损坏办公室

警方迅速清理
**〔此处转录不清〕**

昨天下午，上海劳工战线再次爆发麻烦，杨树浦庆兴丝绸厂的罢工工人与该机构大院内的职员成员及警察发生冲突。
这场骚乱始于下午3时左右，导致两人受重伤不得不送医。当时，约150名罢工者在闲散人员的增援下，前往榆林路484弄的工厂场地，试图进入大院与经理对话。
职员成员试图阻止他们进入，同时打电话请求警方援助。随后发生打斗，期间工厂的一名领班和一名来自榆林路巡捕房的中国巡佐被打成重伤，其他人伤势较轻。办公室的窗户和家具受到一定损坏。来自榆林路的一队警察最终驱散了人群并清理了场地，逮捕了一名作为骚乱头目的男子。秩序迅速恢复，并在工厂周围部署了警方监视。
受伤的领班被送往广慈医院（Sacred Heart Hospital），中国巡佐被送往警察医院。

集会受阻

下午晚些时候，工人们试图在华盛路和华德路交叉口的空置地产上举行集会。榆林路巡捕房再次出动警力，人群毫不犹豫地散去。
昨晚局势平静。
在存在闭厂情况的申悦棉纺厂，鉴于不满工人与管理层之间的谈判结果待定，昨天未报告有新进展。周四早晨发生了一起骚乱，当时一群800人强行冲破了罗宾森路8号七厂的大门，但昨天两家工厂都很平静。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, MARCH 29, 1937

WORKERS STORM MILL, 2 HURT
* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *
Plant Dispute Leads To Riot; Strikes Continue
* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Labor trouble among Shanghai's mill workers again flared up in violence yesterday when some 150 striking employees of the Ching Shing Silk Weaving Factory, 464 Yulin Road, stormed the plant and attacked police officers stationed on the premises.

As a result of the melee, one Chinese detective and one mill foreman were slightly injured. A worker was arrested during the riot.

The storming of the silk weaving factory occurred shortly after 3 o'clock when some 150 men tried to enter the mill and see its management. When they were barred from entering, the workers attacked the officers. Later they rushed into the compound and smashed up part of the office furniture.

Police officers rushed from the Yulin Road station dispersed the mob before further damage could be done. Policemen were posted outside the mill last night to prevent any further violence.

Less than an hour after the riot, a large group of workers gathered at a vacant lot at the corner of Whashing and Ward Roads for a meeting. They were dispersed by police officers.

Meantime, labor disturbance among workers of other local mills remained unsettled yesterday. Employees of the Mayar No. 10 Mill in Chapei were still out on strike despite mediation of the Bureau of Social Affairs and Kuomintang officials.

In Nantao, workers of three mills were on strike yesterday following a demonstration early in the morning. Reports last night stated that the workers at these mills are preparing to resume work this morning.

At the Shing Yue Cotton Mill, Robinson Road, where workers staged a riot Thursday, operation is slated to resume this morning. The striking workers decided to call off the walk-out following a tentative settlement worked out by Kuomintang and Bureau of Social Welfare representatives.

工人冲击纱厂，两人受伤
* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *
工厂纠纷引发骚乱；罢工持续
* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

昨日，上海纱厂工人的劳资纠纷再次演变为暴力事件。位于榆林路464号的庆兴丝织厂（Ching Shing Silk Weaving Factory）约150名罢工员工冲击工厂，并袭击了驻守厂内的警察。

混战导致一名华籍侦探和一名工头受轻伤。骚乱期间，一名工人被捕。

冲击丝织厂的事件发生在下午3点后不久，当时约150名男子试图进入工厂见管理层。在被禁止入内后，工人们袭击了警员。随后他们冲入厂区，砸坏了部分办公家具。

榆林路捕房的警员迅速赶到，在造成进一步破坏前驱散了人群。昨晚，警方在工厂外部署警力，以防止进一步的暴力行为。

骚乱发生后不到一小时，一大群工人聚集在华盛路（Whashing Road）与华德路（Ward Road）转角处的一块空地上开会。他们被警员驱散。

与此同时，昨日本地其他纱厂工人的劳资动荡仍未平息。尽管社会局和国民党官员进行了调解，闸北的梅亚十厂（Mayar No. 10 Mill）员工仍在罢工。

在南市，三家工厂的工人在清晨示威后于昨日罢工。昨晚的消息称，这些工厂的工人正准备于今晨复工。

位于罗宾森路（Robinson Road）的兴裕棉纺厂（Shing Yue Cotton Mill）曾于周四发生工人骚乱，计划于今晨恢复运营。在国民党和社会福利局代表达成初步解决方案后，罢工工人决定停止罢工。
